page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture and running under the KVM hypervisor. The physical hardware comprises an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz with 12 physical cores and 24 dedicated virtual CPUs. System memory totals 192.0 GB, yielding a high memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or attached discrete GPUs, relying on remote block storage for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal an asynchronous performance profile between single-threaded and parallel execution. Single-core processing scores in stress-ng and Geekbench fall within the bottom quartile of evaluated cloud hardware. Conversely, multi-threaded operations exhibit average industry performance, recorded by a multi-core stress-ng score of 17660.86 and a PassMark CPU score of 18392.83. Memory read bandwidth uncached reaches 96.89 GB/sec, supporting standard operational throughput for Redis SET transactions at 16.8 million operations per second and static web serving at 10.83 GB/sec.

The primary operational tradeoff of the ecs.se1ne.6xlarge instance is its lower per-core compute speed against its large RAM allocation. While ill-suited for heavy single-thread compute or large language model prompt processing, the resource density provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy datasets. Appropriate workloads include in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise application backends, and data processing jobs requiring large memory buffers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance equipped with 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs (12 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz, alongside 192.0 GB of RAM. Configured on KVM hypervisors with an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, it includes 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth but lacks local SSD storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmark data demonstrates weak single-threaded performance offset by steady, middle-tier multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics. Key tests highlight throughput of 16.8 million Redis SET operations per second and stable static web serving capabilities. Given its high RAM allocation relative to CPU compute cores, this instance profile offers efficient resource scaling for memory-bound applications, Redis caching tiers, in-memory databases, and web serving backends.
